title: There Is No Eleventh Floor
description: An office worker enters a lift in a ten-floor building. Lynleit finds him on Floor Forty-Seven, with warnings written on his arm and no way home he can trust.
events: A late-working office employee encounters impossible floors, repeated rooms, misleading voices and clocks that cease to agree.
Lynleit finds him on Floor Forty-Seven and tests the stairs, painted boundaries, airflow and door fittings instead of trusting signs.
Her small silver pistol and spare magazine buy time but cannot stop the pursuer. She throws the empty pistol to interrupt its approach.
She puts on protective black leather gloves and tells the witness to cover his head and skin with his jacket. After he loses it, she covers him with her blue coat.

events.text: The coat's hem and lining appear to settle around exposed skin after Lynleit steps away, suggesting an agency the witness cannot explain.

events: Blue flame follows the painted boundary through the distorted stairwell. Lynleit's protected hands remain unburned, but she suffers bleeding, a split lip and tremors.
They stop choosing routes, enter an elevator that appears, and return to the office at 22:55, six minutes after the witness's departure.
Lynleit makes a guarded call. Church envoys examine the witness, have already contacted his relatives, and take him away.
He spends seventeen days in a monastery, returns to work using the stairs, and months later glimpses someone resembling Lynleit across a railway platform.

title: Before the First Bell
description: Lynleit and Fionn attend private negotiations at a church before dawn while their MSF escort waits outside and wonders why.
events: Lynleit and Fionn arrive at a church before dawn for private negotiations.
Felix and Reiner wait outside as the family's security detail.
Lynleit leaves the meeting early and visibly irritated.
Felix and Reiner seek gossip, but Lynleit redirects them with a playful tease.
A report of another disappearance appears while the meeting is in progress.

title: The Last Man Out
description: Captain Heyk leads a specially equipped unit into Vilen's sealed park and becomes its sole survivor.
events: Public disappearances force police to close the park before the government seals it even from them.
Captain Heyk leads a specially equipped paramilitary unit into the park.
Forces the unit cannot understand or explain massacre the squad.
Heyk becomes the sole survivor and is evacuated by the Ducal Guard under Drake's orders.
Grief for his squad follows him into a new role as a Ducal Guard field agent and bodyguard serving Drake and Sherie.
Unusual fog restricts observation and searches in the park; the force that kills the unit remains unexplained.

title: After the Failed Attempt
description: Years of work buy Kyrien proof but no justice. After his failed attack on the Prosecutor General, Lynleit questions him and offers confidential service while his lawyer negotiates the terms.
events: Kyrien funds years of legal work while supporting his mother. Credible evidence is found, but a closed review protects the prosecutor.
After an interval, strangers humiliate his mother in a shop. He decides to kill the prosecutor only after getting her home and attending to her needs.
The newly appointed Prosecutor General survives the dinner attack. Kyrien escapes immediate capture, sees no unmistakable magic, and is detained later.
Lynleit nearly suffers harm at the dinner but conceals her attendance during questioning.
With his lawyer present, Kyrien describes his family's treatment without confessing. Lynleit helps confirm his mother's welfare.

events.text: His refusal to repeat his mother's apology suggests how difficult the humiliation remains to discuss.

events: Lynleit privately recognizes suppression and her need for an ally outside her circle. Kyrien accepts paid confidential work subject to legal review of release, care, and employment terms.
Lynleit tells Felix and Reiner, not Fionn. Reiner trusts her judgment; Felix accepts without trusting Kyrien.

versions.label: v1 · Archived
versions.description: After Kyrien's failed attack on an MSF-protected politician nearly harms Lynleit, she questions him without revealing that she was present and converts his prison risk into a secret alliance.
events: Kyrien's attempt on an MSF-protected politician fails because the target secretly belongs to the Magi world.
Lynleit is present and almost harmed during the attempt, but Kyrien does not know she was there and she never tells him.
Lynleit takes control of his interrogation and offers conditional freedom in exchange for becoming her secret helper.
She recruits him because her intuition warns her that a danger she cannot yet identify is approaching.
Lynleit later tells only Felix and Reiner, while even Fionn remains outside the compartment.
Reiner trusts Lynleit's judgment, while Felix accepts the decision without trusting Kyrien.

title: The Name Left Behind
description: Natalia follows a missing name through the city archive and finds her niece Myka protecting the last surviving clue.
events: Natalia finds a missing page hidden from every archive index.
Myka reveals an unaltered copy carrying Fionn's name beside a future date.
The archive erases the evidence while Natalia attempts to preserve it.

title: The Empty Boats Beneath the Bridge
description: The River Choir, Part I. Kyrien checks the exits, endures four failed watches and boards the empty boats on the fifth. When the river takes hold of the team, the forbidden bank is the only ground he can reach.
events: Kyrien inspects the bridge, locked park barrier and city steps before the covert boat operation.
Four failed watches exhaust the camera windows; a breaking branch and a pale camera interruption remain unexplained.
Lynleit and Kyrien play repeated card games during operational downtime. He watches her hands; she watches his fingers and face.

events.text: Their attention to each other begins to exceed what either needs to win a card game.

events: On the fifth watch, heavy mist interrupts the view across the river. Three wooden boats arrive with fixed rudders and empty tarp-covered holds.
Felix stays ashore while Reiner, Maren, Ivo, Lynleit and Kyrien descend by rope.
Kyrien steadies Lynleit at the waist when the boat shifts and releases her as she catches the rail.
Maren is pulled over the side. Reiner tries to hold her, then enters the water; Ivo follows to help.
Lynleit puts on black gloves and rolls up her sleeves. Kyrien cuts a snagged line before their boat rolls.
Kyrien feels fingers holding his leg but cannot see their source. Reiner, Maren and Ivo move towards the city steps while he struggles towards the park roots.
Kyrien reaches the mud on the park bank without understanding the attack.

versions.title: The Empty Boats Beneath the Bridge
versions.description: A covert MSF inspection of apparently unmanned river shipments collapses when the Drowned Choir attacks from below, leaving Kyrien to witness Lynleit's forbidden water walking from the quarantined bank.
events: Sherie and Drake ask Lynleit to assemble a loyal team and inspect recurring night traffic on the Vilen river.
Several surveillance nights produce no boats while small oddities emerge from the quarantined park.
After the failed watches, Lynleit repeatedly challenges Kyrien to short card games and they learn each other's physical tells.

events.text: Their unfinished rematches and attention to breath, hands, and pauses imply an attraction neither character names or allows to displace the operation.

events: Felix freezes the bridge cameras and remains on the city bank as fallback while Reiner leads Lynleit, Kyrien, Maren, and Ivo down onto the boats.
When a boat shifts, Kyrien briefly steadies Lynleit near the concealed Sparrow holster and releases her before she asks.

events.text: The empty boats, drowned hands, and pale girl imply that the contraband crews were taken before the interception.

events: Reiner, Maren, and Ivo reach the city bank with Felix's fallback line while Kyrien is forced toward the quarantined park bank.
The drowned hands tear away Lynleit's blue suede jacket and drag her underwater until fury releases blue flame through the river.
The river surface holds beneath Lynleit's palm, knee, and boots, allowing her to stand above hands that cannot cross it.

events.text: The pale girl's silence and tilted head imply that Lynleit's survival contradicts the rule by which the Drowned Choir takes people.
Kyrien's careful denial and continued silence imply that he has chosen to protect Lynleit's forbidden ability before either of them openly trusts the other.

events: Lynleit crosses the held surface to the park bank and later sits back to back with Kyrien for warmth among the trees.

title: The Water Beneath Her Feet
description: The River Choir, Part II. Lynleit recounts the failure from the empty hold, the hands beneath the river, and her escape using an ability she has kept hidden.
events: Lynleit questions the empty holds and prepares to end the inspection when Maren is pulled overboard.
She puts on both protective gloves and rolls both sleeves, but holds her flame while rescuers are too close to Maren.
The overturned boat separates her from the team. She sees the city-bound swimmers and Kyrien struggling towards the park.
Hands seize her boots and jacket underwater. Her practiced swimming cannot free her, and her childhood fear of drowning returns.
Blue flame burns the submerged grips. The light exposes hands of different sizes and states of decay; her ordinary blue suede jacket tears away.
The river supports her palm, knee and boots. She recognizes an ability she has secretly practiced at night.
Lynleit fears the Church discovering an act that resembles a forbidden miracle, while still wanting to hear her team.
A silent girl emerges in a dress of dead fish, her eyelids sewn shut with fishing line. Her fingertips touch the water.

events.text: The tilted head and stillness suggest that the girl cannot readily account for Lynleit standing above the hands.

events: The submerged hands cannot reach through the surface beneath Lynleit. She tests her steps backwards towards the park without discovering why.
Lynleit reaches the mud, climbs by a branch and calls Kyrien. She does not know that he watched her crossing.

title: The Wrong Bank
description: The River Choir, Part III. Kyrien watches from the trees, withholds what he has seen and helps Lynleit find a way out of the quarantined park, where something moves above the path.
events: Kyrien reaches the park bank and hides behind a tree while searching the near water for Lynleit.
He watches her rise, stand and walk on the water. The distant pale figure is visible, but its stitched eyes are not.
Lynleit reaches the bank and takes his forearm to climb. They sit back to back while recovering from immersion.
Kyrien deliberately avoids admitting that he saw her standing on the river. He suspects her fear of being seen without knowing the Church reason.
A phone call confirms Reiner, Maren and Ivo reached the city side. Maren reports feeling hands, not seeing their source.
Reiner directs them to the path and warns that the riverbank drops away before the bridge.
On the wet park path Lynleit questions Kyrien again. Both admit fear; she describes the sewn eyelids and dead-fish dress to him.
An elongated shape moves above the path while the supporting branches remain still. Both see it without identifying it.
They keep it in sight while detouring around the bench, then reach the locked barrier and rejoin Felix and Reiner.
All six regroup on the city side. Lynleit reports movement in the park, Kyrien keeps the water walking secret, and their unfinished cards are still in the van.

title: The Nameless Street
description: Lynleit loses Felix during a walk after lunch and follows a child's cries through an impossible street.
events: Lynleit and Felix take an ordinary walk through central Vilen after lunch.
Lynleit finds herself alone, dizzy, and unable to navigate a street that does not obey the surrounding city.
A little girl loses a red balloon and runs away crying.
Lynleit catches the balloon and follows the girl's cries through the labyrinth.
The girl leads Lynleit to a broken fence above the body of a dead boy, then pushes her from the ledge.
Lynleit wakes on a city bench while Felix tries to revive her from an apparent fainting episode.

events.text: The girl's smile and sudden push suggest that her crying was a lure.

title: Doom Has an Address
description: Mikhail's mock blessing becomes a prolonged argument over ancestry, porcelain, and Lynleit's private life. Once she looks away, he lets one silence pass without a joke.
events: Lynleit and Kyrien destroy a Holumn together and complete the final condition of its mechanism.
The Holumn transfers one terminal curse across both identities, causing progressive physical decline and a prognosis measured first in weeks and then in days.
Suppressing the curse in either person fails because the remaining attachment reconstructs it in the other.
The traditional solution requires one of them to die first so the surviving identity is released.
Lynleit rejects the fatal solution, consults other Magi, and searches Magiarchal records and prohibited theurgical procedures for an alternative.

Natalia uses a two-name diagram, her failed decision diary, and her experience after leaving the Academy to explain why a change of identity must go deeper than its description. She introduces the ego hypothesis and quotes Jung.
Lynleit jokes with Natalia, works through the examples, and keeps the diagram; Natalia proposes reciprocal attachment as a possible change, not a guaranteed cure.
Father Mikhail reaches the same conclusion through Church records and tells Lynleit that physical intimacy could work only if an existing attachment changes both identities.
Mikhail names Inanna and describes Lynleit's lineage as preserving a three-thousand-year association with the Cult; she objects to using that history as a personal obligation.

events.text: Lynleit's handling of her cup, increasingly formal objections, and threatened reprisal suggest how personally Mikhail's mock praise has struck her.
Mikhail leaving Lynleit's averted gaze unremarked suggests that he recognizes when his teasing has reached something she cannot easily answer.

events: Lynleit withholds the proposed method from Kyrien and investigates their relationship as a possible procedure.
Lynleit attempts to initiate an encounter but does not fully cross the boundary between them.
The curse begins weakening the following morning and is later gone.

events.text: Lynleit's unread pages and repeated denials suggest that she still wants Kyrien now that the curse is gone.

events: Kyrien suspects a connection between Lynleit’s attempt and their recovery, but she withholds the proposed treatment.
The incomplete attempt and its aftermath change both identities enough for the curse to lose its hold.

title: The Bench under the Lamp
description: An evening walk leaves Lynleit and Kyrien beneath a park lamp. A joke about their failed attempt becomes a private encounter, followed by an unexpected request for his flask.
events: Lynleit and Kyrien walk through the quarantined park after work, lose their way, and stop at a bench beneath a lamppost.
Kyrien takes one small drink from his flask after the long day and returns it to its usual pocket.
Their comfortable proximity and teasing bring up the failed curse encounter months earlier.
Lynleit has spent the intervening months researching intimacy; the opportunity on the bench is spontaneous.
Lynleit rests her head in Kyrien’s lap.

events.text: Lynleit’s satisfaction and claim of successful research indicate progress beyond the earlier failed encounter.

events: Lynleit calls the research successful, and they leave the bench before Kyrien asks whether she intends to win arguments this way.

events.text: Her delayed request for whiskey and refusal to explain suggest an unexpected practical consequence without undoing her satisfaction.

events: Kyrien hands her the flask without pressing for an explanation, and they continue walking.

title: The Shared Night
status: Canon direction · Scene draft with writer gap
description: A shared-dream investigation becomes painfully personal when Sherie discovers that Felix remembers the same nights. Natalia refuses to mistake a dream for a confession.
events: Independent reports describe corresponding dream memories, including violence, grief and intimate encounters, without corresponding bodily injuries.
Natalia briefs Lynleit, Kyrien, Felix, Sherie and Reiner on the Oneiric Confluence and rejects treating dream behaviour as a confession.
Sherie discovers that Felix remembers their recurring sexual dreams. Their discussion exposes the difference between remembered participation and freely chosen action.
Lynleit and Kyrien acknowledge a shared experience without recounting it to the group.
Sherie and Felix test whether they can resist the dream. Recognizing a pressure briefly restores choice, but its return prevents them from treating recognition as a reliable cure.
When they can step away, Sherie does so. They keep their agreement not to touch or kiss, then arrange coffee after waking.
